title: CI: produce signed provenance + terraform module digests and rollback manifests for private installer releases
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds signed provenance bundles, deterministic terraform module digests, and automated rollback manifests to the private-installer release pipeline. Improves traceability of release artifacts and enables safe automated rollbacks for on-prem upgrades.
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require cryptographically verifiable artifacts and a deterministic way to rollback to a known-good installer bundle. This PR extends the private-installer CI to emit signed provenance envelopes for every packaged artifact (helm charts, on-prem tarballs, terraform modules), compute and record stable digests for terraform modules, and generate a rollback manifest that lists the exact artifact URIs and checksums for the previous N releases.

What this changes (high level):
- CI: .github/workflows/release-private.yml now runs a new 'package-and-prove' job after build that packages artifacts into OCI layout, computes SBOM-lite, signs a provenance envelope with the configured KMS key, and uploads to the release bucket.
- Rollback manifests: A new script scripts/generate_rollback_manifest.py aggregates previously-signed release entries and composes a rollback manifest (installer/release/rollback-${version}.json) referenced by the release index.
- Terraform module digests: terraform/modules/installer now produces a module-digest.json containing canonicalized file list and SHA256 digests, and the pipeline records the digest and the module-lock signature in provenance.
- Packaging: scripts/package_installer.sh updated to emit both artifact index and provenance files. installer/provenance/sign_and_bundle.sh encapsulates signing and attestation format (simple envelope + detached signature).
- docs: docs/release/runbook-private-installer.md updated with steps to validate provenance, inspect rollback manifests, and the quick path for manual rollback.

Checklist: [x] CI job added and wired to release workflow; [x] signing step uses KMS key alias and records key fingerprint in provenance; [x] rollback manifest generator produces deterministic ordering; [x] terraform module digests included in release index; [x] runbook updated with validation commands; [x] tests for generate_rollback_manifest script included.

Commits (summary):
- feat(ci): add package-and-prove job and tooling to release-private workflow (Maya Patel)
- feat(prov): add sign_and_bundle script and provenance template for installer artifacts (Maya Patel)
- feat(tf): emit module-digest.json for terraform modules and record in index (Maya Patel)
- feat(rollback): add generate_rollback_manifest.py and integrate with release index (Maya Patel)
- fix(ci): lint/formatting and CI flake fixes (Maya Patel)

Changed areas and small snippets:
- .github/workflows/release-private.yml: adds 'package-and-prove' job that runs on successful build and pushes artifacts to release-staging bucket.
- installer/provenance/provenance.template.json: includes fields: artifact_uri, artifact_digest, packaging_format, sbom_uri, signer_key_fingerprint, created_at, linear_ticket.
- scripts/generate_rollback_manifest.py: reads release index, sorts entries by semantic version, and emits rollback manifest containing up to 5 previous releases with artifact URIs and signed provenance pointers.
- terraform/modules/installer/module-digest.json: canonicalized manifest example: {"files": [{"path":"main.tf","sha256":"..."}],"root_digest":"..."} (canonicalization implemented with stable JSON and sorted file lists).

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam Chen (reviewer): "Can we record the KMS key fingerprint in the provenance envelope so customers can verify which key signed the bundle? Also add a test to assert deterministic ordering of the rollback manifest."
- Maya (author): "Added key_fingerprint to provenance.template.json and updated sign_and_bundle.sh to call aws kms get-public-key when available; added unit test test_rollback_ordering.py that asserts stable sort by semver."
- Sofia Martinez (reviewer): "CI failed lint initially on python script style and missing type hints; also flagged potential large file uploads to release bucket."
- Maya (author): "Addressed linting, added streaming upload with multipart threshold and an abort-on-failure policy. Re-ran pipeline."
- Rajiv Kapoor (approver): "Verified signed envelopes and module-digest canonicalization locally, approved after CI green."

CI details: Initial run had 'flake8' and 'black' failures on generate_rollback_manifest.py which were fixed in a follow-up commit. Integration tests run in the pipeline include: unit tests, packaging smoke test (validate OCI layout), provenance validation (check signature and presence of key_fingerprint), and terraform-module-digest verification. Final CI status: pass.

Edge cases and notes:
- Rollback manifest only references previously-signed releases; we intentionally do not auto-promote unsigned artifacts.
- If KMS is unavailable in a DR path, the pipeline records 'signer_key_fingerprint: null' and the runbook documents manual signing fallback.
- The terraform module digest uses a canonical ordering to avoid churn from filesystem differences across CI runners.

Post-merge: The release pipeline will pick up the new job on next tag push. I ran an end-to-end dry-run using a synthetic tag and verified the produced release index includes provenance URIs and a rollback manifest with two previous entries. Operations/Oncall notified via the post-merge webhook and the runbook link is included in the release ticket.

Merge: Squashed and merged after approvals.
